result:
All the files are in place. Here's a summary of what I found and fixed.

## What was happening

Lumina pivoted from "InboxZap" (inbox cleanup) to an AI meeting assistant, but the migration was half-finished, actively strangling organic traffic:

- **`app/layout.tsx`** still shipped InboxZap's `<title>` and OG tags sitewide, while every actual page was about meetings — a glaring brand/content mismatch for both crawlers and anyone clicking through from search.
- **12 blog posts** (all legacy inbox-cleanup content, confirmed against `gsc/Queries.csv` — "gmail storage full," "unsubscribe from newsletters," etc.) carried nearly all GSC impressions but ranked position 40–60. Why: the blog index fetched posts client-side from a `/api/posts` endpoint that doesn't exist, so Google's HTML snapshot was just a "Loading posts…" spinner with zero links to any post — the posts were orphaned, discoverable only by old cached URLs.
- **`sitemap.ts`** only listed 4 URLs and explicitly `TODO`'d including blog posts, plus it listed `/features` and `/pricing`, which didn't exist as routes at all (404s) — the nav linked to pages that weren't built.
- **`/faq`** permanently redirected to `/#faq`, but no element with `id="faq"` existed anywhere.
- **post-3 and post-7** both targeted "bulk delete emails" with near-identical content, splitting rankings between two pages instead of ranking one well.
- **`/pricing`** was missing a canonical tag (every other page had one); all 12 posts had no meta description.
- Separately: the brand term "inboxzap" still ranks position ~4 with real clicks — those users land on an unrecognizable product with no explanation.

## What I changed

- Rewrote `layout.tsx` metadata to Lumina branding sitewide, added Organization JSON-LD.
- Built real `app/features/page.tsx` and `app/pricing/page.tsx` (single H1, descriptions, canonicals).
- Added an `id="faq"` FAQ section to the homepage (with FAQPage JSON-LD) so the redirect actually resolves, and a one-line "formerly InboxZap" note to catch confused branded searchers.
- Replaced the client-fetch blog with server-rendered `lib/posts.ts` + `app/blog/page.tsx` + `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` — real crawlable links, per-post metadata/canonical/descriptions.
- Merged post-3/post-7 into one stronger guide, 301-redirected the duplicate in `next.config.js`.
- Fixed `sitemap.ts` to include all 11 remaining post URLs plus the real pages, dropping the dead TODO.

## What I didn't do, worth deciding on

The deeper strategic issue: even fixed, those 11 legacy posts target an audience (Gmail/Outlook declutterers) with no overlap with Lumina's actual buyer (teams wanting meeting notes). I'd treat the technical fixes as hygiene, not a growth plan — the real traffic lever is a new content cluster around meeting-assistant queries (meeting minutes, Zoom/Teams transcription, async standups, action-item tracking). Happy to scope that next if you want it.
